title: Brand-anchored surface variants and chart-stroke adaptors for low-light console
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Several console surfaces (panels, cards, dense lists) and chart elements (grid lines, axis strokes, series outlines) show inconsistent contrast and perceived elevation when brand accents are applied in low-light/dark environments. This leads to visual noise and occasional failures against accessibility contrast thresholds for core workflows (query results, billing tables, critical alerts).

Goal: Define a set of brand-anchored surface variants and lightweight chart-stroke adaptors that preserve brand identity while guaranteeing legible contrast and consistent perceived elevation across supported console themes (light, dim, low-light/dark). Provide clear component override rules and token mappings to be consumed by the component library and runtime theme resolver.
acceptance_criteria: Surface variant tokens (surface.brand.*) defined for three elevation tiers with numeric contrast targets and token names matching the console token schema
Chart stroke and axis adaptors implemented as token mappings that support up to 4 brand accent colors without violating WCAG AA for text and critical UI elements
Component overrides documented for primary button, subtle button, table row hover, and card border to use brand-anchored surfaces when customer brand is applied
Design specs and Figma kit uploaded, with annotated contrast checks and example screens for Light, Dim, and Low-Light themes
Hand-off checklist completed and at least one dev story created (ENG-59012) to implement token migration with feature flag
design_notes: Avoid introducing new raw color tokens; instead derive brand-aware surfaces from existing neutral scales using a compositing approach (alpha overlay on neutral frames) to keep runtime layering predictable
Introduce 'brand-surface-anchored' tokens that combine a low-opacity brand tint with base elevations; these tokens are intended for optional brandized deployments only
Chart adaptors should be a thin transformation layer: input accent color -> suggested stroke/outline + dimming factor per theme. Keep adaptors deterministic so runtime can cache mappings.
Button contrast: primary button should prefer high-saturation brand fill on light theme, but switch to neutral-fill-with-brand-accent-outline in low-light to preserve readability
Prioritize table text contrast over subtle brand accents on active rows and selected states (table legibility is critical for power users)
Provide a 'preview safety' flag that disables intense brand overlays for customers who opt into accessibility-first rendering
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Scoping session with PM and engineering; agreed to prototype three surface variants and chart adaptor mapping. Decided to avoid new raw tokens to minimize runtime churn.
2025-02-18: First Figma exploration: created three card options (soft-tint, overlay-tint, neutral-frame) and two chart stroke options. Shared with visual QA for contrast testing.
2025-02-24: Visual QA results: soft-tint fails AA on small text in low-light for some brand palettes. Pivot to overlay-tint + increased elevation cast for critical surfaces.
2025-02-28: PM requested a reduced set of overrides limited to primary/button/table/card for MVP. Added acceptance criteria for feature flag and dev story.
2025-03-02: Engineering asked for explicit numeric contrast targets and example token expressions for runtime. Added explicit mappings and composite formula suggestions to hand-off.
Open: final approval from accessibility reviewer scheduled 2025-03-04
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Brand tints could reduce token reusability and increase token permutations. Mitigation: use derivation/composite rules instead of full token expansion.
Risk: Some customer brand palettes will still fail contrast checks. Mitigation: provide an accessibility preview checker and fall back to neutral rendering when thresholds cannot be met.
Risk: Runtime performance impact if adaptor mapping is computed per-request. Mitigation: cache computed mappings at theme load and persist per-tenant configuration.
Risk: Styling regressions in legacy components. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout and smoke tests for core pages (queries, billing, alerts)
next_steps: Finalize numeric contrast targets and publish token naming convention by 2025-03-04
Complete accessibility review and incorporate feedback (deadline 2025-03-06)
Create ENG stories (ENG-59012) and schedule pairing session for hand-off week of 2025-03-10
Build Figma demo pages showing brand onboarding flow and preview safety toggle
